end2.title: Tempered Flow
end2.text: Mara leaves at first light with a lighter pack he didn't pack himself and a gauntlet that breathes instead of roars. Somewhere beyond the map's edge, a valley marked abandoned is waiting to be wrong.
obj.knock: Find somewhere to stop for the night.
obj.spar: Show Bryn what the gauntlet does.
obj.retune: Bring the gauntlet to Bryn's bench.
obj.supplies: Sort out supplies for the road.
obj.farDoor: Leave by the far door at first light.
hint.knock.1: The house has a door and a bell. Either will do.
hint.knock.2: Use the bell, or open the door.
hint.spar.1: Bryn wants to see the gauntlet working. Talk to her first.
hint.spar.2: Talk to Bryn, then use the training cage.
hint.listen.1: After the sparring, Bryn has a question for Mara.
hint.listen.2: Talk to Bryn and answer honestly; say what he needs once he has said enough.
hint.records.1: Bryn's return pipe has a reading valve. The regulator remembers things.
hint.records.2: Use the regulator on the reading valve.
hint.retune.1: Bryn has offered to work on the gauntlet.
hint.retune.2: Use the gauntlet on Bryn's bench.
hint.supper.1: There's a pot on the hearth.
hint.letter.1: Bryn's dawn courier carries letters. Mara has something to write in.
hint.letter.2: Use the notebook on the courier's pouch.
hint.supplies.1: Bryn asks about supplies over supper. There's more than one way to answer.
hint.supplies.2: Talk to Bryn about supplies and ask her for help.
hint.map.1: Bryn's map shows the route out of Cinderfold country.
hint.map.2: Look at the map on the wall.
hint.farDoor.1: Everything's ready. The far door opens on the road ahead.
line2.secretDoorframe: Scratches on the doorframe, one above another: little couriers' marks, each with a date. People have been stopping here for a long time.
line2.secretDoorframeAgain: There's room for one more mark. I'll leave it for the way back.
line2.secretCrucible: An old crucible, cracked, with two handprints pressed into the clay before it was fired. One big, one very small.
line2.secretCrucibleAgain: Bryn hasn't thrown it out. I don't think she ever will.
line2.gauntletLook: Mum's gauntlet. The cell hums like it's still angry at the crossing.
line2.gauntletTempered: Mum's gauntlet, retuned. The pressure moves through it now instead of slamming into the end.
line2.notebookLook: Mum's notebook. There are blank pages at the back. Enough for a letter.
line2.notebookAfterLetter: Two pages shorter. Oren will complain about my handwriting.
line2.regulatorLook: The regulator, still pulsing against my hip. Slow. Patient.
line2.regulatorAfter: The regulator. It isn't the fault. Something further down the line is. That changes everything.
line2.breadEat: Nell's bread, a day older and still good. I save the crust.
line2.scarfWear: The road's cold. Nell would say put it on. I put it on.
line2.heroLook: Ash to the knees and a gauntlet still too hot. I've had better days.
line2.heroLookAfter: Fed, warm, and the gauntlet's quiet. Who'd have thought.
line2.heroTalk: Keep moving. That's the plan. That's always been the plan.
line2.heroLie: Just for a second. Just... a second.
line2.bellLook: A brass bell on a bracket, green with weather. Somebody polishes the clapper.
line2.doorLook: A heavy door, iron-banded. Warm light round the edges, and the smell of hot metal.
line2.doorLookOpen: The door's on the latch now.
line2.knock: Hello? I'm a courier from Cinderfold. I know it's late.
line2.brynDoor1: Late's the only time couriers ever turn up. Hold on.
line2.maraDoor: I can sleep in the lee of the wall, if you'd rather—
line2.brynDoor2: You can sleep in the lee of my soup. In. You're dripping ash on my step.
line2.windowLook: A lit window. Someone's moving around inside, quick and heavy-footed.
line2.signpostLook: "CINDERFOLD", pointing back the way I came. I don't look at it long.
line2.farPipesLook: The great pipes go on into the haze. The same pipes that pass under home.
line2.roadBackLook: The road back to Cinderfold. Everything I'm trying not to think about is that way.
line2.roadBackGo: No. Not yet. I said I'd carry this to the First Hearth.
line2.valveLook: A valve with a reading glass set into the return pipe's flange. It glows when the pipe is running.
line2.valveLookAfter: The reading glass has gone dim again. It told us enough.
line2.valveUse: I'd rather not open something on Bryn's pipe without Bryn.
line2.recordsNotYet: Hold that thought. First tell me why you swing like that.
line2.recordsAgain: We've read it. Twice. It isn't going to say anything different.
line2.records1: Give it here. The valve reads what a regulator's been feeling, like a doctor reading a pulse.
line2.records2: Huh. Look at the return trace. Your regulator wasn't failing. It was working too hard, because the heat coming back to it was wrong.
line2.records4: Damaged somewhere along the return circuit. Not in Cinderfold. Further out. Your regulator just took the blame.
line2.records5: Then it could be fixed. Properly. Not just patched and prayed over.
line2.benchLook: Bryn's bench: tongs, gauges, a glove worn through at the knuckles, and a bowl of something orange she keeps snacking from.
line2.benchUse: Not my bench to make a mess of.
line2.benchDone: It's done. She says if I keep hitting with it like a hammer she'll take it back.
line2.benchNotYet: I haven't even seen how you use it yet. Rig first.
line2.benchRecordsFirst: Regulator first. I want to know what we're tuning you for.
line2.retune1: Bench. Gauntlet off. No, leave the cell in — I need to feel it run.
line2.retune2: There. It was dumping everything at the knuckles. Now it'll vent through the wrist and keep a little back. Pressure that has somewhere to go doesn't have to hurt anyone.
line2.retune3: It feels... lighter. Like it isn't holding its breath.
line2.retune4: That's Tempered Flow. Use it like that and you'll still have something left at the end of a fight. Supper. Come through.
line2.cageLook: A caged rig on a sprung frame: a brush drum that swings back at whatever hits it.
line2.cageNotYet: It's Bryn's rig. I should ask her first.
line2.sparStart: Go on, then. Hit it like you mean it. I want to see where the pressure goes.
line2.sparAfter1: Stop, stop. You'll crack the cell like that. Every strike, you emptied the whole thing.
line2.sparAfter2: That's how it works. You push until it moves.
line2.stoolLook: A three-legged stool, worn smooth. Exactly where someone would sit to watch the rig.
line2.stoolUse: If I sit down now, I don't know if I'll get up.
line2.coalLook: A crate of good coal. Bryn doesn't do anything halfway.
line2.coalTake: I'm carrying enough heat as it is.
line2.viewLook: The valley drops away under the open side. Lights here and there, far apart.
line2.returnPipeLook: The return pipe runs right through the house. Bryn built her workshop around it on purpose, I think.
line2.returnPipeUse: It's warm. Steady. The way it should be at home.
line2.toBackroomLook: A heavy curtain. Something that smells wonderful is on the other side.
line2.toBackroomNotYet: Back room's for after work. Work first.
line2.toRoadLook: The open side, and the road out. It's dark now.
line2.toRoadGo: Not in the dark. Not with the gauntlet like this.
line2.pouchLook: A courier's pouch on a peg, flap open. Bryn's dawn courier leaves before first light.
line2.pouchLookAfter: My letter's in there, under someone's order for crucible clay.
line2.pouchTake: It isn't mine to take. Only to put something in.
line2.letterAlready: Oren will have it by tomorrow evening. Probably reading it out loud.
line2.letter1: Oren. I'm at a tempering house past the crossing. I'm all right.
line2.letter2: I'm not just all right. I'm tired, and I was scared on the crossing, and the smith here fixed my gauntlet and made me eat. The regulator isn't the fault. Something further on is. I'm going to find it.
line2.letter3: There. Folded, in the pouch. It's the truest letter I've ever written.
line2.map1: Bryn's map: the route out of Cinderfold country in her neat hand. And there, past the next crossing, a valley with a cross through it. "Abandoned."
line2.map2: The ink of that cross is newer than the rest.
line2.mapAgain: "Abandoned." Then why does the road still go there?
line2.farDoorLook: The far door. The road ahead starts on the other side of it.
line2.leaveLetter: Not yet. I should let Oren know I'm all right.
line2.leaveSupplies: I haven't sorted anything for the road. Supplies. Food. Cells.
line2.leaveMap: I should know where I'm going before I go.
line2.leave1: First light. Thank you, Bryn. For all of it.
line2.leave2: Don't thank me, come back through. Bring me a story and an empty pack.
line2.shelfLook: Bryn's supply shelf: cells, cord, dried food, a tin of something labelled only "NO".
line2.shelfTake: I'm not going to raid her shelf. I could ask.
line2.hearthLook: A stone hearth with a pot on the fire. Something with beans in it. A lot of beans.
line2.hearthLookAfter: The pot's lighter by two bowls. Bryn ate both of hers standing up.
line2.eatAgain: If I eat any more I'll need a bigger pack.
line2.eat1: Oh. That's... I hadn't noticed how hungry I was.
line2.eat2: You never do. Nobody who swings like you do ever notices.
line2.tableBread: I put Nell's bread on the table. Bryn takes a piece and says Cinderfold bakers are wasted on Cinderfold.
line2.tableLook: A table with a bowl and a loaf. Two chairs, only one of them ever used.
line2.cotLook: A cot under a heavy blanket, by the far door. She's given me the warm side of the house.
line2.cotUse: Five minutes. The blanket smells of coal smoke and lavender. Bryn snorts from the hearth.
line2.brynBread: Nell's bread? Put it on the table, we'll share it. I don't take a courier's rations.
line2.brynItem: That's yours. Keep hold of it.
line2.brynLook: Bryn: broad as a door, sleeves rolled, a burn scar on one forearm and a grin that doesn't take no.
line2.brynLookEvening: Bryn, apron off for once, eating beans straight from the pot with a ladle.
dlg2.bryn.intro1: Right. Let me look at you. Courier, ash to the knees, gauntlet humming like a kettle about to go. Crossing gave you trouble.
dlg2.bryn.intro3: "Fine" is what people say right before they fall over in my workshop. I'm Bryn. I tune gauntlets for a living.
dlg2.bryn.intro4: Before I touch that one, I want to see it work. The rig's in the cage. Go on.
dlg2.bryn.waiting: Cage. Rig. Hit it. I'll be right here judging you.
dlg2.bryn.ask1: You hit that rig like it was a wall between you and somewhere else.
dlg2.bryn.ask2: So I'm not going to tell you you're reckless. I'm going to ask. What are you trying to get through so quickly?
dlg2.choice.rush: Nothing. I'm just used to being quick.
dlg2.choice.home: Cinderfold's cold. Everyone there is waiting on what I'm carrying.
dlg2.choice.alone: If I slow down, I'll have to think about doing this on my own.
dlg2.choice.name: I'm scared it all comes down to me. I need to know I'm not the only one holding it.
dlg2.choice.later: Can we talk about it later?
dlg2.bryn.rush1: Quick and spent aren't the same thing.
dlg2.bryn.rush2: Quick people still breathe. You hit like you'd forgotten how.
dlg2.bryn.home1: So you're carrying a whole village's winter on one hip.
dlg2.bryn.home2: No wonder you swing like you're late. You think you are.
dlg2.bryn.alone2: Going fast means you never have to notice how far from home you are. I know. I built a house on a road so I'd never have to notice either.
dlg2.bryn.name2: Thank you for saying it plainly. Most people take three bowls of soup to get there.
dlg2.bryn.name3: Saying it out loud doesn't make it smaller.
dlg2.bryn.name4: No. But now there are two of us looking at it. Let me read that regulator you keep touching, then bring the gauntlet to the bench.
dlg2.bryn.later: Rig's not going anywhere. Neither am I.
dlg2.bryn.toRecords: Regulator first. Use it on the reading valve, up on the pipe.
dlg2.bryn.toBench: Bench. Gauntlet. Now, before you talk yourself out of it.
dlg2.bryn.evening: Sit. Eat. Then tell me what you're short of for the road.
dlg2.choice.supplies: I'll make a list of what I need for the road.
dlg2.choice.letter: Is there any way to send word home?
dlg2.choice.valley: That valley on your map. The one marked abandoned.
dlg2.bryn.supplies1: A list. And then you'll sort it, and pack it, and check it twice by lamplight, and fall asleep sitting up.
dlg2.choice.askHelp: Could you put my supplies together? I'd rather sleep.
dlg2.bryn.manage: You will. You always do. That's the trouble.
dlg2.bryn.askHelp2: Food, cells, cord, and a tin of the good stuff. Packed by dawn. You sleep.
dlg2.bryn.letter1: My dawn courier leaves before you're awake. Pouch is by the far door.
dlg2.bryn.letter2: Write to that Oren of yours. Tell him the truth, not just "fine".
dlg2.bryn.valley1: Marked abandoned. Doesn't mean empty. Maps lie about places nobody bothers to visit.
dlg2.bryn.valley2: Somebody crossed it out recently. Make of that what you like.
dlg2.bryn.night: Go on. Bed. The road will still be there at first light; you'll just be in better shape for it.
line2.toWorkshopLook: The curtain back to the workshop. The rig's still swinging slightly in its cage.
note.secretDoorframe: Couriers' marks on Bryn's doorframe, one above another, each with a date. People have stopped here for a long time.
note.secretCrucible: An old cracked crucible in Bryn's workshop with two handprints in it: one big, one very small.
